title: Handle OneDrive read-only directories during safe worktree removal
requirements: Before git worktree remove, clear only the Windows read-only attribute throughout the exact verified task worktree and its exact Git-owned .git/worktrees/<ID> metadata directory; never touch the primary checkout tree or unrelated Git metadata.

Reject symbolic links, junctions, path escapes, unexpected metadata paths and non-DONE or dirty worktrees before attribute changes; allow ordinary OneDrive reparse attributes that are neither symlinks nor junctions.
Retain PIPE-011 whitelist cleanup, post-clean status check and implementation ancestry check, then remove the worktree and record cleanup normally.
Add cross-platform regression tests plus a Windows read-only directory scenario and document the OneDrive behavior.
acceptance: Safe cleanup succeeds for a DONE clean worktree whose directories are read-only, without generic git clean or forced worktree removal.
Primary files and unrelated .git/worktrees metadata are unchanged, while links, wrong paths and unknown ignored files continue to fail closed.
Focused pipeline tests, whitespace validation, self-review, finish and cleanup pass.

shared_paths_approval.reason: Follow-up safety fix for the verified OneDrive read-only failure in controller-owned worktree cleanup.
